title: Probability, permutations and combinations
description: Dice, cards and coins, arrangements with repeated letters, circular seating and committees.

questions.prompt: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that the numbers add up to 7?
questions.explanation: Six of the 36 equally likely outcomes give 7: (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), (6,1). 6/36 = 1/6.

questions.prompt: In how many different ways can the letters of LEVEL be arranged?
questions.explanation: 5 letters with L twice and E twice: 5! / (2! × 2!) = 120 / 4 = 30.

questions.prompt: In how many ways can a committee of 3 be chosen from 8 people?
questions.explanation: Order doesn't matter in a committee: C(8, 3) = (8 × 7 × 6) / (3 × 2 × 1) = 56. 336 counts ordered choices.

questions.prompt: A fair coin is tossed 3 times. What is the probability of getting at least one head?
questions.explanation: Use the complement: the only outcome with no heads is TTT, with probability 1/8. So P(at least one head) = 1 − 1/8 = 7/8.

questions.prompt: A bag has 4 red and 6 blue balls. Two balls are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
In how many ways can 5 people sit around a round table, if only their order around the table matters?
questions.explanation: Rotations of the same seating are identical, so fix one person and arrange the other 4: 4! = 24.

questions.prompt: How many 3-digit numbers with all digits different can be made from the digits 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5?
questions.explanation: 5 choices for the first digit, 4 for the second and 3 for the third: 5 × 4 × 3 = 60.

questions.prompt: One card is drawn from a standard 52-card deck. What is the probability that it is a king or a heart?
questions.explanation: 4 kings + 13 hearts − 1 king of hearts counted twice = 16 cards. 16/52 = 4/13.

questions.prompt: In how many ways can a captain and a vice-captain be chosen from a team of 11?
questions.explanation: The two roles are different, so order matters: 11 choices for captain, then 10 for vice-captain: 110.

questions.prompt: A two-digit number (10 to 99) is chosen at random. What is the probability that it is divisible by 7?
questions.explanation: The multiples of 7 from 14 to 98 are 7 × 2 up to 7 × 14: 13 numbers. There are 90 two-digit numbers, so 13/90.
